title: Warwickshire Access to Food LLM pilot underperforms a simpler classification method
summary: Warwickshire’s LLM achieved 63% classification accuracy versus 95% for a simpler method. Faster food-access mapping remains intended; improved food access is not established.
account: Warwickshire County Council tested a locally hosted Llama 2 model to classify businesses by size and food availability, aiming to identify areas with limited access to affordable, nutritious food. Accuracy was 63%, compared with 95% for a simpler method. Processing took up to 1.5 hours per output. The council anticipated that further fine-tuning could save staff time on manual searches. Its evaluation demonstrates neither time savings nor improved food access. Inconsistent model labels leave the exact configuration unclear.
purpose: Reduce manual search work when mapping access to affordable, nutritious food.
system: Locally hosted Llama 2 business-classification proof of concept
domain: Food access and local government analysis

ratings.reason: Staff time savings remain intended. The unfavorable accuracy and processing results do not establish an operational improvement.
Residents with limited access to healthy food are intended beneficiaries. Improved food access remains unproven.

ai_role.statement: The LLM classified businesses by size and food availability. The intended savings in staff time and improvements in food access remain unproven.

evidence.citation: Warwickshire County Council internal pilot evaluation, published by the Local Government Association, February 3, 2025. The account provides no independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Warwickshire County Council: “Access to Food” – exploring LLMs for citizen needs

produced_by: A locally hosted LLM classified businesses but underperformed a simpler method.
must_hold: Further development and comparative testing would be needed. Conditions sufficient for a beneficial outcome remain unknown.
